items.notes: 2026-11-04: run 2 passed on the numbers. The branch then conflicted with master (PrometheusHTTPProtocolAPI.cpp: master added StoragePrometheusQuery::applySettingsForPrometheusQuery), so I rebased onto fd328d4baedf and moved the cache setup into that helper. Related upstream: 118801. 2026-11-05: run 3 passed; merges cleanly with master 39b9f2d5aedb; final review Approve (nit: spill_state not moved on adoption). Optional before submitting: an HTTP API test of x + x + x with use_index_for_in_with_subqueries=0&max_threads=1 (the no-wait path is otherwise covered only by the gtest); it would need another build. My recommendation: submit as is.

items.title: Stop evaluating an ALP parameter pair once it cannot beat the best one
items.summary: run 2 passed: small-block INSERT of decimal-like values 2.2x faster (-54.6%), codecs_float_insert ALP rtn -9.9%, nothing slower; same bytes
items.head: d6f173c6e3d3228867a5815d441e561fc572a94a
items.claim: Run 2 (head d6f173c6e3d3): same bytes as master. In the encoder-alone harness under clang 20 at the release flags, Float64 decimal-like values take 38-93% less encode CPU, full-precision and random doubles 1-9% less, Float32 6-88% less; nothing is slower. End to end (prediction): small-block rtn about -45%, small-block rnd about -2%, codecs_float_insert ALP rows faster or unchanged.
items.pass_if: 05480 (4 pinned sizes) passes on A and B; 04612 and 05054 pass on B; codecs_float_alp_small_blocks rtn at least 30% faster and rnd not significantly slower; codecs_float_insert ALP rtn significantly faster, and no ALP row of codecs_float_insert slower than the slowest unchanged-codec row (NONE, LZ4, ZSTD, DoubleDelta, Gorilla, FPC) of the same run.
items.notes: Run 1 (d4c58e0009b4) failed: codecs_float_insert ALP mon +10.2%, seq +4.0%. Cause: clang vectorizes master's scoring loop; the per-value cut-off made it scalar, which loses where pairs are cut late (values that are not decimals). My harness used g++ and missed it. Fix 32eb990cdbb9 (cut-off only under RD_SIZE_THRESHOLD_LIMIT, each sample seeded with the previous best pair + 1); 05480 gained two pinned sizes (bd592b96a5d7, ded70dddecf1, d6f173c6e3d3) and a chassert. Price: the small-block rnd gain shrinks from -16% to about -2%. Run 1's A binary (c189bd99fbda) can be reused. If a debug build is at hand, run 05480 on it once (chassert). ALP is GA on master since 129732: enable_alp_codec is a no-op there, harmless in the test. Merges cleanly with master 2f701ba6d627. After a pass I add T1's end-to-end number to the changelog entry.

items.pass_if: Follow ab-plans/sink-lazy-pipelines.md. Pass: T1 (your ingest-at-scale jobs, 1M series, stock table, 6 cells per side, core sets swapped) at least 5% lower server CPU per sample on B with p < 0.05; M1 on B <= 0.3 us per sample; C1 (bench/sink-lazy-pipelines/contents.sh after the same handler_cpu.sh run, async_insert 1 and 0) equal on A and B; no guard (G1 latency, G2 each dashboard query with its query text in the row, G3 flush CPU, E1 async_insert=0) significantly slower; 05875 and 05876 pass on B; on A 05875 fails in exactly its 2 InsertQueriesWithSubqueries lines and 05876 passes (its reference is master's output); also_run and integration tests pass on B.
items.notes: Handoff #27 (your prototype). Commit 1 = the prototype's 14 lines. Commit 2 (preflight rounds 1-3): the sink's constructor checks INSERT on exactly the inner tables and columns its pipelines will write, so grants and missing inner tables behave as on master at the same point (the prototype alone had moved that check into the async flush: wait_for_async_insert = 0 -> success, then data dropped). Still moved to the first block / the flush: checks of MVs on the inner tables, the insert delay and too-many-parts error, share locks (remote write waits for the flush). Lab (2 vCPU, master 521c4bcb7b94): the 4 unused inner INSERTs cost 1.1 ms CPU per INSERT (empty INSERT 2,557 us vs 1,452 us MergeTree control); remote-write handler 4.9 ms per 2,000-sample request. Overlap: your upstream PR 123144 and valerypetrov's 121062 also create some target pipelines on demand (open); whichever lands second keeps first-chunk creation. Idea 2 (skip the handler's outer InterpreterInsertQuery) not done: needs a block path in executeQuery, ~0.7% CPU. Branch can't be compiled here: 05875's reference is master's output with the 2 predicted lines changed; 05876's is master's output.
